   282→def _join_expansion(validator: Validator, instances: Any) -> Iterator[Any]:
   283→    if len(instances) == 0:
   284→        return
   285→
   286→    if len(instances) == 1:
   287→        for value, _, _ in validator.resolve_value(instances[0]):
   288→            if not isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
   289→                raise ValueError(f"Incorrect value type for {value!r}")
   290→            yield [value]
   291→        return
   292→
   293→    for value, _, _ in validator.resolve_value(instances[0]):
   294→        if not isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
   295→            raise ValueError(f"Incorrect value type for {value!r}")
   296→        for values in _join_expansion(validator, instances[1:]):
   297→            yield [value] + values

   300→def join(validator: Validator, instance: Any) -> ResolutionResult:
   301→    # quick validations
   302→    if not validator.is_type(instance, "array"):
   303→        return
   304→    if not len(instance) == 2:
   305→        return
   306→
   307→    for delimiter, delimiter_v, _ in validator.resolve_value(instance[0]):
   308→        if not delimiter_v.is_type(delimiter, "string"):
   309→            continue
   310→        for values, values_v, _ in validator.resolve_value(instance[1]):
   311→            if not values_v.is_type(values, "array"):
   312→                continue
   313→            try:
   314→                for value in _join_expansion(values_v, values):
   315→                    yield delimiter.join([str(v) for v in value]), values_v, None
   316→            except (ValueError, TypeError):

   360→def _sub_parameter_expansion(
   361→    validator: Validator, parameters: dict[str, Any]
   362→) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
   363→    parameters = parameters.copy()
   364→    if len(parameters) == 0:
   365→        yield {}
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    if len(parameters) == 1:
   369→        for key, value in parameters.items():
   370→            for resolved_value, _, _ in validator.resolve_value(value):
   371→                yield {key: resolved_value}
   372→        return
   373→
   374→    key = list(parameters.keys())[0]
   375→    value = parameters.pop(key)
   376→    for resolved_value, _, _ in validator.resolve_value(value):
   377→        for values in _sub_parameter_expansion(validator, parameters):
   378→            yield dict({key: resolved_value}, **values)

   381→def _sub_string(validator: Validator, string: str) -> ResolutionResult:
   382→    sub_regex = re.compile(r"(\${([^!].*?)})")
   383→
   384→    def _replace(matchobj):
   385→        nonlocal validator
   386→        for value, c in validator.context.ref_value(matchobj.group(2).strip()):
   387→            if not isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
   388→                raise ValueError(f"Parameter {matchobj.group(2)!r} has wrong type")
   389→
   390→            validator = validator.evolve(
   391→                context=validator.context.evolve(
   392→                    ref_values=c.ref_values,
   393→                )
   394→            )
   395→            return str(value)
   396→        raise ValueError(f"No matches for {matchobj.group(2)!r}")
   397→
   398→    try:
   399→        yield re.sub(sub_regex, _replace, string), validator, None
   400→    except ValueError:
   401→        return

   404→def sub(validator: Validator, instance: Any) -> ResolutionResult:
   405→    if not (
   406→        validator.is_type(instance, "array") or validator.is_type(instance, "string")
   407→    ):
   408→        return
   409→
   410→    if validator.is_type(instance, "array"):
   411→        if len(instance) != 2:
   412→            return
   413→
   414→        string = instance[0]
   415→        parameters = instance[1]
   416→        if not validator.is_type(string, "string"):
   417→            return
   418→        if not validator.is_type(parameters, "object"):
   419→            return
   420→
   421→        for resolved_parameters in _sub_parameter_expansion(validator, parameters):
   422→            resolved_validator = validator.evolve(
   423→                context=validator.context.evolve(
   424→                    ref_values=resolved_parameters,
   425→                )
   426→            )
   427→            yield from _sub_string(resolved_validator, string)
   428→
   429→        return
   430→
   431→    # its a string
   432→    sub_parameters = REGEX_SUB_PARAMETERS.findall(instance)
   433→    parameters = {}
   434→    for parameter in sub_parameters:
   435→        if "." in parameter:
   436→            parameters[parameter] = {"Fn::GetAtt": parameter}
   437→        else:
   438→            parameters[parameter] = {"Ref": parameter}
   439→    for resolved_parameters in _sub_parameter_expansion(validator, parameters):
   440→        resolved_validator = validator.evolve(
   441→            context=validator.context.evolve(
   442→                ref_values=resolved_parameters,
   443→            )
   444→        )
   445→        yield from _sub_string(resolved_validator, instance)
   446→        # yield from _sub_string(validator, instance)

   450→    if not validator.is_type(instance, "array"):

   394→def url_has_newer_version(url):
   395→    """Checks to see if a newer version of the resource at the URL is available
   396→    Always returns true if using Python2.7 due to lack of HEAD request support,
   397→    or if we have no caching information for the local version of the resource
   398→    """
   399→    metadata_filename = get_metadata_filename(url)
   400→
   401→    # Load in the cache
   402→    metadata = load_metadata(metadata_filename)
   403→
   404→    # Etag is a caching identifier used by S3 and Cloudfront
   405→    if "etag" in metadata:
   406→        cached_etag = metadata["etag"]
   407→    else:
   408→        # If we don't know the etag of the local version, we should force an update
   409→        return True
   410→
   411→    # Need to wrap this in a try, as URLLib2 in Python2 doesn't support HEAD requests
   412→    try:
   413→        # Make an initial HEAD request
   414→        req = Request(url, method="HEAD")
   415→        with urlopen(req) as res:
   416→            # If we have an ETag value stored and it matches the returned one,
   417→            # then we already have a copy of the most recent version of the
   418→            # resource, so don't bother fetching it again
   419→            if (
   420→                cached_etag
   421→                and res.info().get("ETag")
   422→                and cached_etag == res.info().get("ETag")
   423→            ):
   424→                LOGGER.debug(
   425→                    "We already have a cached version of url %s with ETag value of %s",
   426→                    url,
   427→                    cached_etag,
   428→                )
   429→                return False
   430→
   431→    except NameError:
   432→        # We should force an update
   433→        return True
   434→
   435→    # The ETag value of the remote resource does not
   436→    # match the local one, so a newer version is available
   437→    return True

   567→def _translate_types(types: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
   568→    """
   569→    Return compatible types. This is an adventitious result
   570→    meaning a string could be an integer.
   571→
   572→    Args:
   573→        types (Sequence[str]): The types
   574→
   575→    Returns:
   576→        bool: If any type of source is compatible with any type in the destination
   577→    """
   578→    compatible_types = []
   579→    for t in types:
   580→        if t == "string":
   581→            compatible_types.extend([t, "number", "boolean", "integer"])
   582→        if t == "integer":
   583→            compatible_types.extend([t, "number", "string"])
   584→        if t == "boolean":
   585→            compatible_types.extend([t, "string"])
   586→        if t == "number":
   587→            compatible_types.extend([t, "string"])
   588→        else:
   589→            compatible_types.append(t)
   590→    return compatible_types

   598→    """

   601→    Args:

   603→        destination_types (str | Sequence[str]): The destination types
   604→
   605→    Returns:
   606→        bool: If any type of source is compatible with any type in the destination
   607→    """
   608→    if not strict_types:
   609→        source_types = _translate_types(ensure_list(source_types))
   610→    destination_types = ensure_list(destination_types)
   611→
   612→    if any(schema_type in source_types for schema_type in destination_types):

   103→class _Transform:
   104→    def __init__(self) -> None:
   105→        self._collections: MutableMapping[str, str] = {}
   106→
   107→    def transform(self, cfn: Any) -> TransformResult:
   108→        """Transform the template"""
   109→        return [], self._walk(cfn.template, {}, cfn)
   110→
   111→    # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
   112→    def _walk(self, item: Any, params: MutableMapping[str, Any], cfn: Any):
   113→        obj = deepcopy(item)
   114→        if isinstance(obj, dict):
   115→            # adjust keys if needed
   116→            if params:
   117→                for k, v in item.items():
   118→                    _, new_k = self._replace_string_params(k, params)
   119→                    if new_k != k:
   120→                        del obj[k]
   121→                        obj[new_k] = v
   122→
   123→            for k, v in deepcopy(obj).items():
   124→                # see if key matches Fn::ForEach
   125→                if re.match(FUNCTION_FOR_EACH, k):
   126→                    # only translate the foreach if its valid
   127→                    foreach = _ForEach(k, v, self._collections)
   128→                    # get the values will flatten the foreach
   129→                    for collection_value in foreach.items(cfn, params):
   130→                        flattened = self._walk(
   131→                            v[2], {**params, **{v[0]: collection_value}}, cfn
   132→                        )
   133→                        for f_k, f_v in flattened.items():
   134→                            if f_k not in obj:
   135→                                obj[f_k] = f_v
   136→                            else:
   137→                                raise _ValueError(
   138→                                    f"Duplicate {f_k} while doing transformation",
   139→                                    f_k,
   140→                                )
   141→                    del obj[k]
   142→                elif k == "Fn::ToJsonString":
   143→                    # extra special handing for this as {} could be a valid value
   144→                    return obj
   145→                elif k == "Fn::Sub":
   146→                    if isinstance(v, str):
   147→                        only_string, obj[k] = self._replace_string_params(v, params)
   148→                        if only_string:
   149→                            return obj[k]
   150→                    if isinstance(v, list):
   151→                        only_string, obj[k][0] = self._replace_string_params(
   152→                            v[0],
   153→                            params,
   154→                        )
   155→                        if only_string:
   156→                            return obj[k][0]
   157→                        if len(v) == 2:
   158→                            obj[k][1] = self._walk(v[1], params, cfn)
   159→                elif k == "Fn::FindInMap":
   160→                    try:
   161→                        mapping = _ForEachValueFnFindInMap(get_hash(v), v)
   162→                        map_value = mapping.value(cfn, params, True, False)
   163→                        # if we can resolve it we will return it
   164→                        if isinstance(map_value, tuple([list]) + _SCALAR_TYPES):
   165→                            return map_value
   166→                    except Exception as e:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
   167→                        # We couldn't resolve the FindInMap so we are going to
   168→                        # leave it as it is
   169→                        LOGGER.debug("Transform and Fn::FindInMap error: %s", {str(e)})
   170→                    for i, el in enumerate(v):
   171→                        v[i] = self._walk(el, params, cfn)
   172→                    obj[k] = v
   173→                elif k == "Ref":
   174→                    if isinstance(v, str):
   175→                        if v in params:
   176→                            return params[v]
   177→                    elif isinstance(v, dict):
   178→                        r = self._walk(v, params, cfn)
   179→                        if isinstance(r, str):
   180→                            if r in params:
   181→                                return params[r]
   182→                        obj[k] = r
   183→                else:
   184→                    sub_value = self._walk(v, params, cfn)
   185→                    # a sub object may be none or we have returned
   186→                    # an empty object.  We don't want to remove empty
   187→                    # strings "" or 0 (zeros)
   188→                    # Remove `or sub_value == {}` for issue #2896
   189→                    if sub_value is None:
   190→                        del obj[k]
   191→                    else:
   192→                        obj[k] = sub_value
   193→        elif isinstance(obj, list):
   194→            for i, v in enumerate(obj):
   195→                obj[i] = self._walk(v, params, cfn)
   196→        return obj

   198→    def _replace_string_params(
   199→        self,
   200→        s: str,
   201→        params: Mapping[str, Any],
   202→    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
   203→        pattern = r"(\$|&){[a-zA-Z0-9\.:]+}"
   204→        if not re.search(pattern, s):
   205→            return (True, s)
   206→
   207→        new_s = deepcopy(s)
   208→        for k, v in params.items():
   209→            if isinstance(v, dict):
   210→                if sys.version_info.major == 3 and sys.version_info.minor > 8:
   211→                    v = (
   212→                        hashlib.md5(
   213→                            json.dumps(v).encode("utf-8"), usedforsecurity=False
   214→                        )
   215→                        .digest()
   216→                        .hex()[0:4]
   217→                    )
   218→                else:
   219→                    v = hashlib.md5(json.dumps(v).encode("utf-8")).digest().hex()[0:4]
   220→            new_s = re.sub(rf"\$\{{{k}\}}", v, new_s)
   221→            new_s = re.sub(rf"\&\{{{k}\}}", re.sub("[^0-9a-zA-Z]+", "", v), new_s)
   222→
   223→        if isinstance(s, str_node):
   224→            new_s = str_node(new_s, s.start_mark, s.end_mark)
   225→
   226→        return (not (bool(re.search(pattern, new_s))), new_s)
